Maya to run a 1-hour latency/throughput vet in HyperStrata staging (provisioning windows: week of 2029-01-22)
HyperStrata to provide quota and expected qps by 2029-01-16

meeting_header: Date: 2029-01-12 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood Solutions), Priya (HyperStrata Partnerships), Derek (HyperStrata Infra), Sofia (HyperStrata Channel), Kenji (Edge Ops)
summary: Introductory technical/partnership discovery between Redwood and HyperStrata. Main goals: validate runtime compatibility with HyperStrata provisioning model, understand security/compliance gaps for channel resell, define pilot benchmarks and commercial touchpoints. Agreed next steps include a short Redwood-run staging benchmark, security deep-dive, and draft SOW for pilot.
topics: integration architecture (VPC / peering / private control plane)
GPU provisioning and instance types (burst vs reserved)
security & compliance requirements (KMS, SOC2, audit logs)
transcript:
00:00 Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, appreciate it. we're hoping to run through how Redwood might fit into HyperStrata's marketplace and any constraints you have.
00:14 Priya (HyperStrata): Thanks Jordan, excited. Quick context: we run a hybrid GPU marketplace, partners can onboard compute offers into our catalog. interested in low-friction runtime integration and a channel revenue share model.
00:28 Maya (Redwood): Hi all, I'm Maya, I'm the SE on this. i want to focus on the technical pieces — networking, runtime, and the test plan we can run in your staging.
00:40 Derek: from infra side i'm Derek. primary things: how do you handle private tenants, can we pin models, and how is KV cache persisted across restarts — we have bursty demand and nodes preempt often.
00:57 Maya: good q. Redwood supports model pinning on Dedicated and we have prefix/KV caching that can be either in-memory or backed to a persistent store in Private deployments. for marketplace we usually recommend in-memory with warmup probes, but we can evaluate persistent KV to avoid cold-start regen.
01:20 Kenji: follow up — if we do persistent KV what are latency implications? our SLA for interactive agents is 120ms p95.
01:33 Maya: persistent KV will add a small tail, but our compilation + kernel selection minimizes token compute time. our approach: fast-path in-memory cache for hot prefixes; fallback to persistent on eviction. can usually hit 120ms p95 for short seq use cases with appropriately sized GPUs and batching.
01:53 Priya: what do you need from us to validate?
01:58 Jordan: the checklist — fleet specs, sample qps, security requirements, and a staging endpoint we can push to. i'll send a checklist after this.
02:07 Sofia: commercial — we want to see how pricing + margins work. are you ok with a reseller program and volume discounts?
02:15 Jordan: yes, we have a channel pricing ladder and a dedicated reseller contract. we'll include initial banding in SOW.
02:23 Derek: on the provisioning model: HyperStrata has ephemeral GPU pools and also long-lived reserved nodes. we want Redwood to be able to route requests to the cheapest compatible variant but fall back to high-SLA nodes if latency spikes.
02:40 Maya: that fits our smart routing model — policy-driven: by latency, cost, or tier. we can register model variants and define routing fallbacks. key is the model compatibility (fp16/quantized) across node types; if you have older GPU types we might need to use a quantized variant or lower-precision kernel.
02:58 Derek: we have mixture — A100s and some older 40GB V100 equiv.
03:06 Maya: fine, we can test kernel selection heuristics. but for large context generative workloads we recommend newer tensor cores; for embeddings and rerank lower precision on older GPUs is often fine.
03:20 Priya: security: our enterprise customers require SOC2 + KMS encryption for customer keys, also audit logs for any model calls that touch PII. how do you expose logs and keys?
03:33 Noah (Redwood): we offer KMS integration and can encrypt KV persistence using customer-managed keys. logs can be exported to an HTTP endpoint or S3 with fine-grained access controls; we also provide token-level tracing in Console for debug windows.
03:50 Derek: need to confirm at what granularity you store prompt/response content.
03:57 Maya: default redaction settings mask sensitive fields; for Private deployments we can toggle retention and ensure no persisted payloads. we'll document specifics in the security packet.
04:12 Priya: can you support a private control plane? some partners require non-shared control plane for compliance.
04:19 Jordan: yes, Redwood Private option supports a customer-managed control plane with VPC peering or on-prem bundles. that is typically an enterprise add-on.
04:28 Priya: good. next, performance benchmarks — what does Redwood need to run a credible staging run?
04:34 Maya: at minimum: sample models list, target qps distribution, typical prompt length, and a staging endpoint where we can spin up our runtime. ideally a small, isolated GPU pool (2-4 GPUs) for smoke tests. we'll bring a micro-benchmark that measures p50/p95 token latency and throughput under different batch sizes.
04:54 Derek: we can provision a 4-node A100 staging cluster for a week.
05:00 Maya: perfect. can you also share any network egress limits and whether NAT is allowed — our runtime may pull layers and quantized artifacts during startup.
05:12 Derek: nat is allowed in staging, in prod we prefer private artifact hosting.
05:18 Maya: noted.
05:22 Priya: question on billing integration — HyperStrata wants usage to flow into our metering system so we can settle partner payouts. what does Redwood expose?
05:31 Jordan: we have a usage API and can stream per-tenant per-model tokens and cost estimates. we also export CSV/JSON daily reports. we can integrate with your metering webhook.
05:43 Sofia: reseller margins: are there minimum commits? how do you handle overage?
05:49 Jordan: for channel pilots we avoid minimums, but for production resellers we do tiered commitments. overage is billed at the agreed band rate; SOW will clarify.
05:58 Kenji: operational concerns: how fast can you scale during a demand spike? our agents see sudden bursts during business hours.
06:06 Maya: autoscaling is configurable; Dedicated pools can burst to extra capacity if available, otherwise routing to cheaper variants or other regions is possible. for market models we recommend pre-warming during expected peaks.
06:22 Derek: curious about quantization — do you have recommended quantized runtime for older GPUs?
06:28 Maya: yes, we maintain quantization profiles per model architecture. for Llama-family variants we use int8 or gptq-style; accuracy tradeoffs are in the profile and can be tuned per workload.
06:42 Priya: anything we should run on our side to make the test quicker?
06:46 Maya: provide a small canonical prompt set, success metrics (latency, pass/fail rate, CVR), and a sample customer tenant to isolate. also share fleet telemetry so we can match infra to expected loads.
06:58 Jordan: i'll attach a short spreadsheet with the benchmark template and sample prompts after call (link: https://redacted/hyperstrata-benchmark-template).
07:10 Derek: security deep dive — who at Redwood owns SOC2 artifacts and where do we find penetration test results?
07:18 Noah: our security team owns SOC2. we can share the SOC2 report under NDA and provide penetration test summaries. i'll loop in our security PM on the follow-up.
07:30 Priya: timeline — we aim to pilot in Q1. is that feasible?
07:36 Jordan: yes, a Q1 pilot is feasible if staging benchmarks are green and we finalize SOW in two weeks.
07:44 Sofia: on the commercial side, channel enablement — do you provide co-marketing assets or enablement for our partner sales?
07:51 Jordan: yes, we have partner kits, demo scripts, and joint case study frameworks. we'll include an enablement packet.
07:59 Kenji: any gotchas around GPU licensing or specific drivers we should know?
08:06 Maya: drivers matter for some kernel optimizations; we'll supply a recommended OS image and docker runtime config. licensing is per-model for some closed models — typically for open-source variants we're fine.
08:20 Derek: can Redwood support a cross-region fallback? our catalogue is multi-region and we need failover paths.
08:27 Maya: yes, smart routing can prefer local region but fallback to other regions with model compatibility checks. replication of KV may be eventual, so consider the consistency model for stateful agents.
08:44 Priya: are there existing partners using similar marketplace integrations? any public references?
08:50 Jordan: we've integrated with a few channel partners but cannot disclose all publicly; i'll share anonymized case notes.
08:58 Sofia: what are the main risk areas you see for this integration?
09:03 Maya: three: 1) fleet heterogeneity causing model compatibility/workflow fragmentation, 2) networking/perf tails from persistent KV or cold-starts, 3) data residency or compliance restrictions for certain customers. all addressable but need planning.
09:20 Derek: for the pilot, can Redwood run an A/B with a quantized variant vs full FP16 to show cost delta?
09:27 Maya: yes, we can do that in staging — same prompts, two model variants, show cost/token and quality metrics.
09:34 Priya: perfect. let's recap action items.
09:38 Jordan: recap: i'll send checklist, SOW draft, and benchmark template. Maya will prepare benchmark harness and staging script. Derek will provision staging cluster and share fleet profile. Sofia will draft channel commercial outline. Noah will introduce security PM for SOC2/doc sharing.
09:55 Priya: thanks everyone. one last thing — commercial cadence: after we review SOW and security we'll aim to sign pilot terms.
10:03 Jordan: great. we'll target the dates we discussed. thanks all.
51:30 [call ends — recording stopped]
